content.title: Lakers get positive injury news on Luka Doncic, concern remains for Austin Reaves
content.text: The Lakers expect Luka Doncic to return before Austin Reaves as the NBA Playoffs loom. As long as they can keep their season alive, the Los Angeles Lakers are looking forward to the return of Luka Doncic. But in the case of Austin Reaves, the franchise remains uncertain that it will happen as early as possible. Appearing on Run It Back, Lakers reporter and insider Jovan Buha revealed that LA expects Doncic to return from his injury recovery before Reaves as the NBA Playoffs loom. "He obviously went to Spain to get treatment. They're hoping that could shave off a few days, or even up to a week. ... Austin, it was four to six weeks," Buha shared. Doncic (Grade 2 left hamstring strain) and Reaves (Grade 2 left oblique injury) got injured at the worst possible time for the Lakers heading to the final week of the past regular season. As it is, Doncic has taken a much more aggressive approach by heading to Europe to seek medical treatment and faster hamstring recovery. It remains to be seen how their respective recoveries will further progress, but the Lakers can only be more focused on playing and going all out against the Houston Rockets in the opening round of the NBA Playoffs. As Doncic and Reaves have been ruled out for Game 1 already and will remain uncertain to play for the entire series, LeBron James and LA are expected not to come out without a fight despite being the clear underdogs.
